items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So, he came, even without liking the music, he came with books, be-bop books by Dizzy and Charlie Parker and Monk all that. And more LPs and all that, and we ended up loving that music.

ctx.x: You talked about your father and the music that influenced him, such as Artie Shaw and Benny Goodman and basically from what is referred to as the Swing style of Jazz. At what point did you begin to get a sense of modern developments of Jazz?

That’s a very good question. My father was a constant force in my life, you know; he was incredible. He came—I remember like today—he had a, one of those silver turntables. So he came with those little LPs, those small LPs, with the face of Charlie Parker, a very young Charlie Parker and that be-bop bowtie and that was totally different image than Ellington and all those people have; it’s totally different. He say, “I want you to hear this.” The day before we were listening to Artie Shaw and Ellington and Benny…
with be-bop and I make it a living after that, and it’s been a living for the last 40 years. It was a blessing, that language that Dizzy and Parker—
